jobs.title: Technical Customer Support
jobs.description:
QuickMail is a cold email and LinkedIn outreach platform for markets you can't afford to burn. Our customers can't easily replace leads that land in spam, which is why deliverability matters more to us than anything else. We have been running since 2014, and we pioneered deliverability technology such as Inbox rotationâ¢ and deliverability AIâ¢.

The Role

We are hiring a technical customer support person with an owner's mentality.

You will own support for QuickMail and Mailflow, our deliverability add-on. There is no first or second line. You are the first and last person our customers talk to.

Customers count on you to solve their problems and find the real cause when something breaks. You work closely with engineering, and you tell the founder what we need to know to make the product better: where the friction is and where the opportunities are.

The role covers the help desk, system health checks, testing new releases before they ship, and leading the weekly team meeting. It takes excellent communication, solid technical understanding and sharp critical thinking.

This is not a script-reading job. Most tickets involve deliverability, DNS records, LinkedIn automation or campaign setup. You dig into customer accounts in our Support Dashboard, reproduce the issue, then decide what to do and how to explain it to the customer.

We are a remote team spread across time zones. Most routine tasks have a written guide with a checklist, so you know what done looks like. You are expected to refine and improve those processes. When something new comes up, you work out the most efficient way to handle it.

If you want a lot of autonomy across many areas, real responsibility and a fast-paced environment, this role is for you.

What Work Looks Like

You own two things: customers get unstuck fast, and the product stays reliable.

Every day

  • Set the day's support priorities and work the Help Scout queue for QuickMail and Mailflow. Triage, resolve, and dig deeper when a ticket needs it.
  • Check the support dashboard: job queue, event-stream latency, blacklist status, newly purchased domains. If something is off, investigate, diagnose, and drive it to resolution.
  • Review fraud alerts and disable accounts that are scams or abusing the platform.

Delighting customers

  • Comfortable jumping on calls with customers, building rapport fast, and setting them up for success.
  • Update the changelog and help articles based on what shipped and what customers asked.
  • Share customer feedback with the team, ask happy customers for reviews and case studies, and watch NPS for testimonial candidates.

Making support smarter with AI

  • Improve the AI support agent. Review its answers, fix the docs it drew from when it is wrong, and contact the customer when its reply was off.
  • Write and maintain automated tests, built with AI, that try to break staging before customers do.
  • Use the MCP connections we have in place (Helpscout, GitHub, Postmark, and others) to get an accurate picture of support and find the next thing worth improving.

Keeping the product solid

  • Gatekeep releases. New fixes and features land on staging every week. Test them, confirm when staging is ready to ship, and think through how existing and new users will be affected.
  • Report bugs as GitHub issues with everything the developer needs: steps to reproduce, screenshots or a Loom, and any GraphQL or console errors.
  • Captain red alerts. When a core feature breaks (emails not sending, login down), confirm it, alert the team on Slack or Telegram, update the status page every 30 minutes, keep affected customers informed, and drive the fix. Then run the retrospective so it does not happen twice.

Running the week

  • Lead the weekly team meeting in MonsterOps: issues written up, to-dos done, numbers updated.
  • Keep rock status and KPIs current in MonsterOps.

Tools you'll use: Helpscout, our Support Dashboard, Sidekiq, GitHub, Slack, Telegram, MonsterOps, Outline, MxToolbox, Postmark, Bento, TidyCal, Fathom, Visual Code and Claude.

Who You Are

  • You build rapport fast. You are warm, positive, and relatable in writing and on calls.
  • You are a good communicator. Externally, you can show warmth, empathy and care. Internally, you are able to communicate clearly and concisely about important things.
  • You can operate with minimal instructions. You understand a short brief without every detail spelled out. You can prioritize well (especially when you have a lot on your plate), and get things done without hand-holding.
  • You are comfortable on video. You are natural on live calls with Zoom and Meet, and on recorded video through tools like Loom.
  • Your teammates can always count on you. You say what you'll do and you do what you said.
  • You act with a constant sense of urgency. You can execute fast and find new ways to improve your productivity.
  • You are resourceful. You use all the tools at your disposal to get great results.
  • You have a low ego. You don't take offense easily and you handle disagreement as a discussion, not a personal attack.
  • Growth mindset. You are positive about new workflow/process/product/tool changes. You love giving and receiving positive and negative feedback without getting defensive.
  • Hours that overlap with East coast US and UK, where most of our customers are.

A Plus If You Have

  • Experience with customer facing work, or if you don't have it, tell us why you are perfect for this role.
  • Working knowledge of deliverability and LinkedIn outreach. Warmup, DNS, inbox rotation, DKIM, SPF, Outlook and Gmail technical setup. We can teach this, but a head start helps.
  • Comfort with agency setups. Workspaces, guest seats, inbox purchases and what happens when an agency loses a client.
  • Light data skills. You can pull numbers from Help Scout or our MCP to back up what you report.
  • An eye for happy customers. You notice them and ask for testimonials and case studies at the right moment.

How We Work Together

You'll work directly with the founder and with our lead developer.

Working with the founder can be intense. Here is what that looks like in practice:

  • Replies are short and can come across as harsh. If something written lands badly or isn't clear, ask.
  • Direction can change. The founder may say one thing, then something different a few days later as they learn more. When that happens, check what changed and adapt.
  • Information should be short and to the point. Lead with what matters, then give more details if asked.
  • The founder can stay frustrated about a problem until it's solved. That's something they are aware of and working on. You'll do well here if you can stay calm and focused when the pressure is on.
  • The team often thinks fast and interrupts each other when discussing ideas. If that would bother you, this role probably isn't for you.

This role suits someone with high emotional intelligence, who doesn't take things personally, asks when something is unclear, and keeps many things moving at once.

Your schedule can be flexible. If you have a martial arts class every Thursday at 3 pm, go and make up the time later. In return, on the rare occasion the team needs your help on a weekend, we ask you to be flexible too.

Benefits

  • Contract type: full-time or part-time
  • Compensation: $2,500 to $4,000 USD per month, depending on experience and location. US-based hires will work as independent contractors (1099).
  • Start date: negotiable

About the job

Job Title: Director, Payment Integrity

Reports To: Vice President, Operations

This is an exempt position reporting to the Vice President, Operations. The Director of Payment Integrity is responsible for the Quality Assurance, Grievances & Appeals, and Fraud, Waste & Abuse teams. This role functions as both the director setting strategy for these departments and the direct supervisor managing day to day operations. This position interfaces with all departments of SIHO as well as external stakeholders, vendors, and customers. The ability to interact with all levels of SIHO staff and external parties with a high level of professionalism, while adapting quickly between multiple high priority items, is essential.

Brief Description of Duties:

  • Directly supervise and manage the Quality Assurance, Grievances & Appeals, and Fraud, Waste & Abuse teams, including day to day oversight, staffing, and performance management
  • Read, research, and interpret federal and state regulations governing grievances and appeals, and translate regulatory requirements into practical, actionable process changes
  • Continuously monitor and improve grievances and appeals processes to ensure ongoing compliance with CMS and state regulatory requirements
  • Support the claims and benefit configuration quality assurance program, including developing and delivering training and education for staff

  • Interact directly with customers as needed
  • Work with SIHO Legal and key leadership on special cases and external inquiries from CMS, the Indiana Department of Insurance, law enforcement, and others

  • Lead or support key corporate and departmental compliance initiatives, including SOC audits, CMS Part C Reporting and ODAG, and others as assigned

  • B.S. degree or equivalent work experience in a healthcare operation

  • Strong understanding of federal and state regulations related to grievances and appeals, including CMS and state Department of Insurance requirements

  • Proficient in Excel with the ability to analyze data and draw actionable insights

  • Experience with SIHO systems including the HSP claims system
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office suite products including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook

All positions are subject to change based on the needs of the business.

jobs.description:
About Magic Eden and Dicey
Magic Eden reached unicorn status in just 9 months after launch, one of the fastest in history. We built a category-defining NFT marketplace from scratch and proved we know how to move fast. Now we're doing it again. Dicey is our crypto casino and sportsbook platform, targeting the $180B+ iGaming and sports betting markets.

We're a small, fully remote team. We ship fast, we're hands-on with our data, and we're rebuilding how a growth team operates around AI from the ground up.

The role
Most of the iGaming industry competes on acquisition. Almost nobody has figured out personalized retention, knowing who a player is, what they need right now, and what would actually change their behavior this week. That's the problem you'll own.

This role focuses on the full post-signup journey: expanding our player segmentation framework, designing and running targeted offers and campaigns, and owning the P&L lever that comes with it. It's explicitly AI-native. You'll build workflows, agents, and pipelines to run lifecycle campaigns that would have taken a whole team two years ago. Half the job is identifying the right problem. The other half is running the experiments to find the answer.

What you'll do

  • Own retention and monetization as a growth loop. Set the targets, find the leverage, and drive the numbers for everything that happens after a player signs up

  • Own the player segmentation framework. Today it's value and risk. You decide how it evolves, what signals feed it, and how the rest of the company uses it

  • Build the AI-native growth stack. Analysis, agents, and automated pipelines that surface segments, generate offer candidates, and run campaigns with minimal manual work

  • Design and ship targeted offers for specific segments and moments: reload bonuses, lossback, wager bounties, challenges, win-back sequences. Size them, spec them, ship them, measure them

  • Spend real time in our data warehouse and on-chain data finding patterns and turn them into campaigns before anyone else does

  • Expand the signals we have on players: on-chain activity, status-match programs, social account linking, and whatever else you can think of

  • Run the campaigns. Email, in-app, Telegram, whatever the channel. You're hands-on with it, with AI doing the heavy lifting

  • Partner with engineering and design to ship the product surfaces that make all of this repeatable

What we're looking for

  • Strong intuition for player psychology and incentive design. Experience in gambling, gaming, fintech, or consumer marketplaces helps. Genuine curiosity about why people behave the way they do is required

  • Deeply analytical. You can go from a vague question to a clean cohort cut yourself, without waiting on a data scientist

  • AI-native by default. You already use AI to write queries, build analyses, and automate your own work and you want to push that much further

  • High output with good judgment. You generate a lot of ideas and know which ones are worth testing first

  • Bias to do it yourself. You're comfortable sending the email, running the query, and writing the spec, not just briefing others

  • Comfortable with ambiguity. There's no playbook here, you'll be building it

Backgrounds that tend to fit

  • Growth PM at a data-heavy consumer company

  • MBB consultant who wants to move into product and own outcomes, not just advise on them

  • Product Minded Data scientist or analyst who wants to ship, not just report

Why this is interesting

  • Competitive, top-of-market compensation

  • You're defining what a growth PM looks like in an AI-native company, there's no inherited playbook

  • Personalised retention is where the industry is going and we're building it early

  • Real ownership: a segmentation framework, a product surface, and a P&L lever, with a direct line to the founding team

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.description:
About the role

Linkup is the web search engine built for AI. Our infrastructure crawls, indexes and serves the live web to AI agents, and it’s scaling fast.

We’re looking for a top‑tier Machine Learning Engineer to join Linkup and work hand‑in‑hand with our CTO, Denis Charrier, and the rest of the tech team.

Your core responsibilities will be to:
Design, train and ship ranking and retrieval models for AI agents

  • Design, train and ship ranking and retrieval models for AI agents

  • Bring new ranking signals into the engine, beyond pure relevance

  • Build the evaluation framework that tells us what really improves search quality

  • Optimize model serving for latency and GPU cost

  • Turn customer and benchmark feedback into ranking improvements, with clear before/after numbers

     
 

Requirements

You’re a great match if you:

  • Are excited to help build Google for AI agents- and believe in Linkup’s mission

  • Have strong hands-on experience in information retrieval, ranking or search in production.

  • Build rigorous evals and check the data behind every number

  • Care about latency, cost and reliability as much as model quality

  • Thrive in a fast-paced, high-ownership startup environment

 

Example Projects

  • Ship a new ranking model to production and prove the gain on our eval sets

  • Push our models to the next level: better answers, lower latency, lower cost per query

  • Build and maintain the evaluations framework that measures every change to our search engine

 

Our Stack

Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face, vLLM, Ray, Spark / Databricks, Vespa, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, Terraform

Details

The ideal candidate will play a central role in our engineering team, partnering closely with the founders. The models you ship will decide what thousands of AI products read every day.

We offer a flexible remote‑work policy- see the details here.

Join us and leverage your expertise to push the boundaries of AI!

 

About Linkup

 

Our Vision

We believe in a future of AI agents and the agentic web. These digital entities can create more value for humanity than we ever could alone, but they depend on the internet to operate, collaborate, take action, and gather information.

AI agents need web search. To perform well, they require information that is current, reliable, and context‑specific—not the diffuse, steadily aging knowledge frozen at their last training cut‑off.

Modern web search is built for humans, not AIs. Instead of trusted facts, it serves links, ads, and click‑bait. People want visually engaging pages; AI systems need structured truth. An AI can absorb oceans of data, while human attention barely skims the surface. Humans think visually and intuitively; AI reasons in latent space.

Web 2.0 is sunsetting. The deck is being reshuffled, and the Bing‑Google search oligopoly is crumbling. Indexing ever more pages is no longer the goal; semantically organizing facts for AI systems is. In the coming agentic web, Google’s ad‑driven model has no natural home.

Search for AI must be rebuilt from the ground up. We are reconstructing the web as a rigorously structured knowledge layer, mapping every concept, entity, and claim into a coherent semantic graph. This foundation delivers verified facts and rich context to AI instantly, unlocking faster reasoning, higher accuracy, and radically more useful answers for everyone.

Humans search Google; AI searches Linkup.

 

Our Mission

Reality never stands still, and neither should intelligence. Linkup reconnects language models to a living stream of verified facts, ensuring AIs remain as current and insightful as the world they serve.

Our mission is to deliver the world’s freshest, most trusted knowledge to AIs.

 

Our Culture

Our culture is built on the following values:

  • Mission. We believe we play a critical role in building the agentic web. We are 100% committed to our mission of bringing the reality of the world to AI agents.

  • Speed. We build fast, we build to last. We get things done, well.

  • Ownership. We empower every team member to take ownership of their projects, ensuring they see them through to successful completion.

  • Teamwork. Our strength lies in our unity. We rely on one another and embrace our diversity as a core asset.

  • Humility. We maintain low egos, showing respect for others and continuously learning from their insights and experiences.

We expect all team member to take an active role in shaping our company culture.

 

Our Team

We are a small technical team, working shoulder to shoulder to build the web of agents.

A bit more about our 3 co-founders:

  • Philippe Mizrahi- Led the development of Lyft’s Autonomous Vehicles marketplace. Previously launched Amundsen, an open source search engine.

  • Denis Charrier- Founding Engineer at Niland, an audio search company (acquired by Spotify), then Staff Engineer at Spotify. 15y of software development experience.

  • Boris Toledano- Led robotics at Carrefour, after 3y at McKinsey & Co working on public affairs and digital transformation.

The role

As a Member of Technical Staff focused on Machine Learning, you will ship models, training infrastructure, harnesses and evals end-to-end: designing, building, and launching the tech that makes Ash differentiated as a specialized model for mental health, to change a billion minds and lives.

As a core member of a small but highly skilled team, we expect you to act as an owner and to care passionately about delivering value to our users and ultimately to make people's lives better. We are looking for builders who care deeply about the quality of their work and want to ship things that make a real difference in people's lives. We care more about how you think and build than your specific background. If you're a great engineer who's curious about ML, we'd love to hear from you.

About You

As Constructor.io’s Sales Development Representative (SDR), you’ll be crucial to driving lead generation activities for Constructor. You’ll be expected to become intimately familiar with Constructor’s product offering and key differentiators in the search space. You’re looking to contribute in an entrepreneurial environment and will enjoy access to the founders and leaders in other functional groups.

You’ll work with our outbound automation system to find leads, send emails, use Linkedin Sales Navigator, generate interest, and schedule sales calls. As the point of first contact in our sales process, you’ll be the face of Constructor to new business opportunities. You’ll qualify leads, gather as much information about the prospect as you can, and work with our sales team to close the sale. If you’re awesome, you’ll grow into an Account Executive position by taking on progressively more account responsibilities.

 

About Us

Constructor is the next-generation platform for search and discovery in ecommerce, built to explicitly optimize for metrics like revenue, conversion rate, and profit. Our search engine is entirely invented in-house utilizing transformers and generative LLMs, and we use its core and personalization capabilities to power everything from search itself to recommendations to shopping agents. Engineering is by far our largest department, and we’ve built our proprietary engine to be the best on the market, having never lost an A/B test to a competitive technology. We’re passionate about maintaining this and work on the bleeding edge of AI to do so.

Out of necessity, our engine is built for extreme scale and powers over 1 billion queries every day across 150 languages and roughly 100 countries. It is used by some of the biggest ecommerce companies in the world like Sephora, Under Armour, and Petco.

We’re a passionate team who love solving problems and want to make our customers’ and coworkers’ lives better. We value empathy, openness, curiosity, continuous improvement, and are excited by metrics that matter. We believe that empowering everyone in a company to do what they do best can lead to great things.

Constructor is a U.S. based company that has been in the market since 2019. It was founded by Eli Finkelshteyn and Dan McCormick who still lead the company today.

 

About the Position

  • Take ownership of building top-of-funnel sales opportunities for the sales team by sourcing and qualifying business prospects.

Harvey’s Legal Engineer - Product Specialists are experienced lawyers from top-tier firms who leverage their legal expertise to help customers seamlessly integrate Harvey into their daily workflows—driving adoption, increasing utilization, and supporting long-term expansion and renewal. jobs.title: Solutions Engineer
jobs.description:
About Ultralytics:

At Ultralytics, we commit to relentless innovation in the AI space and seek team members who resonate with our ambition to produce the world's best YOLO AI models. If you're obsessed with AI, eager to make an impact on the world, and thrive in dynamic, high-intensity environments, we invite you to apply for a position on our team.

🌍 Join the team powering the future of vision AI
Hello, hola, 你好, こんにちは, नमस्ते, hallo, bonjour! Thanks for stopping by — we know your time is valuable, so here's what makes Ultralytics special.

⚡ Who we are
At Ultralytics, we're on a mission to simplify AI for everyone. As the linkcreators of the world's leading Ultralytics YOLO models, we empower millions of developers, researchers, and companies worldwide to build state-of-the-art computer vision applications.

Following our $30M Series A round, we're expanding rapidly across our global hubs. This is an opportunity to join a fast-scaling, high-performance team that's redefining the future of vision AI — where ambition meets impact, and ideas become reality.

We move fast. We build boldly. We execute with purpose. And we do it together.

💼 About the role
As a Solutions Engineer, you'll turn complex computer vision problems into production systems built on YOLO. You'll lead technical discovery, design architectures, build benchmarks and proof-of-concepts, and guide customers from their first conversation to deployed models.

You'll work across Sales, Customer Success, Product, and Engineering while partnering directly with customers in manufacturing, retail, security, robotics, and beyond. This is a hands-on role for an engineer who enjoys writing Python, training and optimizing models, deploying across cloud and edge, and owning outcomes throughout the customer lifecycle.

If you thrive on ambiguous problems, direct customer contact, and turning technical possibilities into measurable results, you'll fit right in.

🚀 What you'll do
Technical discovery and solution design

  • Own technical discovery, translate customer needs into architectures, and define measurable success criteria.

  • Evaluate customer data, recommend models, and design training, inference, and deployment strategies.

  • Lead technical qualification and solution design alongside Account Executives and Customer Success Managers.


Prototyping and deployment

  • Build Python prototypes with YOLO, OpenCV, PyTorch, and Docker.

  • Create benchmarks, integrations, and production-ready training and deployment workflows.

  • Deploy solutions across Linux, macOS, Windows, cloud, and edge environments.

  • Diagnose performance, data quality, inference, and hardware acceleration challenges.

  • Use the Ultralytics documentation and YOLO guides to deliver reliable customer outcomes.


Customer engagement and enablement

  • Deliver technical demos, workshops, architecture reviews, and proof-of-concepts that move opportunities forward.

  • Explain machine learning clearly to engineers, operators, executives, and other non-technical audiences.

  • Build trusted relationships and manage technical stakeholders from evaluation through production.


Ecosystem contribution

  • Turn customer solutions into reusable examples, deployment guides, integrations, and documentation.

  • Share feedback with Product and Engineering to improve the YOLO ecosystem.

  • Engage developers through the Ultralytics community and GitHub organization.


📈 What success looks like

  • 3 months: Ramped on the YOLO stack and customers, co-running discovery, and delivering your first demos and project kickoffs.

  • 6 months: Owning technical discovery and POCs end to end, unblocking live deals or at-risk accounts, and earning trust from the AEs and CSMs you support.

  • 9 months: Converting technical evaluations into wins or saves, shipping reusable assets, and providing actionable feedback to the wider organization.

  • 12 months: Becoming the technical partner AEs and CSMs want on their biggest accounts, with POCs that convert and referenceable customer deployments.


🧠 Skills and experience
Core requirements

  • Strong Python and practical experience with YOLO, OpenCV, PyTorch, and computer vision.

  • Experience training, optimizing, evaluating, and deploying machine learning models.

  • Comfortable with Docker, Git, REST APIs, Linux, cloud platforms, and edge workflows.

  • Experience deploying across Linux, macOS, and Windows environments.

  • Proven ability to deliver technical demos, workshops, architecture reviews, and POCs.

  • Strong communication skills with both technical and executive audiences.

  • Independent ownership, urgency, resilience, and results in a high-performance startup environment.

  • Passion for AI, open source, and helping customers achieve real outcomes.


Nice to have

  • Kubernetes, CUDA, TensorRT, ONNX, Jetson, or other edge accelerators.

  • Experience with MLOps, model monitoring, CI/CD, or observability.

  • Familiarity with AWS, Azure, GCP, serverless systems, or managed inference platforms.

  • Experience integrating OpenAI or Anthropic APIs into customer tools.

  • Open-source contributions or experience supporting developer communities.

  • Knowledge of Ultralytics YOLO workflows and production computer vision solutions.


🌟 Why this role

  • Real impact: Your solutions will power vision AI in production across systems used by millions of devices.

  • Demand you don't have to manufacture: YOLO is the world's most popular computer vision model, and customers already come to us looking to do more with it.

  • Build at the source: Work directly on top of the YOLO ecosystem with clear lines to Product and Engineering.

  • A team that ships: Join a fast-moving, high-standard team that values results over routine.

  • Customer ownership: Stay involved beyond the demo and see your technical work reach production.


🚫 What this isn't
This isn't a slideware Solutions Engineer role. You won't hand off after the demo or hide behind a deck — you'll build the solution, get it deployed, and own the technical outcome throughout the client lifecycle.

🌟 Cultural fit
At Ultralytics, we set bold goals and execute with speed, precision, and teamwork. We're driven by hard work, ambition, and resilience — building fast, learning constantly, and delivering measurable impact.

You'll thrive here if you:

  • Take ownership and deliver results with focus and accountability.

  • Combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution.

  • Value excellence, grit, and creativity in equal measure.

  • See collaboration as the foundation for meaningful progress.

💰 Compensation and benefits
We reward excellence and impact — not just tenure or title.

  • Competitive compensation: Competitive compensation packages

  • On-site collaboration: Work with passionate builders in one of our global hubs (London).

  • Flexible working hours: We value results over routines.

  • Generous time off: 24 vacation days, your birthday off, plus local holidays.

  • Tech & tools: Work on cutting-edge AI projects that power millions of devices.

  • Gear: Brand-new Apple MacBook Air/Pro, Apple Studio Display, and AirPods Pro 3.

  • Learning & development: Dedicated budget for personal and professional growth.

  • High impact: Your work will shape the future of vision AI.


👉 Check out Ultralytics careers and our office locations to learn more about our culture, values, and teams.

🌎 Where and how you can work
We believe great work happens where passion meets purpose.

  • This is a full-time, on-site role based in London, UK.

  • Applicants must have legal authorization to work in the country of application.

  • You will report to the Head of Customer Success and Implementation.

What we offer:

Cutting-Edge, Next-Generation AI Computer Vision Technology: Contribute to building cutting-edge computer vision AI models based on the YOLO framework.

Impactful Work: Shape the future of AI-powered solutions that transform industries.

Collaborative Culture: Join a talented and passionate team that values open communication and innovation.

Ultralytics Handbook

Comprehensive guide to our company's mission, vision, values, and operational practices. This handbook is designed to provide key insights and resources for our (future) team members, collaborators, and community to align with Ultralytics' core principles.

Link: https://handbook.ultralytics.com/

You will join at the moment when the hard engineering questions become real product decisions: how do we make a highly capable robotic hand reliable, manufacturable, serviceable, and simple enough to deploy on a real shop floor?

The Role

You design the mechanics of our robotic hands — from the kinematics of a single finger to a complete hand ready for series production.

Multiple drives, gear trains, tendons, tactile sensors and electronics have to fit into a human-sized envelope while surviving hundreds of thousands of cycles. Every millimetre matters, and almost every design decision affects another discipline.

You work hands-on between CAD, test rig and workshop, and report to the CTO.

What you will do:

  • CAD design. Design components, mechanisms and assemblies within tightly constrained envelopes, owning the design from concept through production release.

  • Mechanism & kinematics. Design finger and thumb kinematics, tendon and spindle drives, joints and bearings. Calculate motion envelopes, trajectories, gripping forces and transmission ratios.

  • Calculation & validation. Validate designs through structural and fatigue calculations, FEA, tolerance stack-ups and GD&T before parts are manufactured.

  • Material selection. Select and qualify materials for lightweight structures, wear surfaces, tendons and elastomeric gripping surfaces, and characterise their behaviour under real loads and contact conditions.

  • Assembly design. Design assemblies for efficient assembly, adjustment-free interfaces, serviceability and repair. Specify the required fixtures and tooling.

  • Design for manufacturing. Design for the intended manufacturing process from the outset — machining, injection moulding, sheet metal, additive manufacturing — balancing cost, tolerances and production volumes.

  • Prototyping & testing. Build prototypes, design test rigs and endurance setups, run cycle and load tests, and drive failures to root cause.

  • Documentation & release. Create drawings and BOMs, manage design changes and configuration, and support product development reviews.

  • Suppliers & production. Work with machine shops, material suppliers and manufacturing partners from first prototype through pilot series and production ramp-up.

  • Cross-functional integration. Work closely with Electronics, Sensors and Software to align packaging, interfaces and load paths across the complete system.

What you bring:

  • Degree in mechanical engineering, mechatronics, precision engineering, or a comparable qualification.

  • 5–10 years of experience in mechanical design of precision mechatronic products, including at least one product taken through to series production.

  • Advanced 3D CAD skills in CATIA, NX, SolidWorks, Creo or comparable systems, with confident 2D drawing creation and GD&T.

  • Strong understanding of mechanism design: linkages, gear trains, bearings, shafts, power transmission, backlash and stiffness.

  • Experience with FEA, structural and fatigue analysis, and tolerance calculations as part of everyday design work.

  • Strong knowledge of material selection for lightweight, high-load and wear-critical components.

  • Practical DFM/DFA experience across multiple manufacturing processes.

  • Hands-on mentality — you build the prototype, run the test and analyse the broken part yourself.

  • Fluent in English and German.

Bonus:

  • Experience with robotic hands, grippers, prosthetics or similarly highly integrated mechanisms.

  • Experience with compact drive trains, including planetary, harmonic or cycloidal gearing, spindle drives and actuator integration.

  • Experience with elastomers, soft goods, injection moulding of complex geometries or compliant structures.

  • Experience integrating tactile or force sensors into mechanical structures.

  • Experience with multi-body simulation or topology optimisation.

Zipline is the world's largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. 

Our customers include the world's largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we've built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

One day you may be advising on a complex Nigerian employment or a healthcare regulatory issue in Cote d'Ivoire; the next, developing compliance training for teams across Africa or helping the business navigate export controls, sanctions, anti-corruption, and other cross-border legal risks.

Account Management is where DataSnipper grows. Our EMEA Accounting AM team manages a book worth tens of millions in ARR across the region's leading audit and accounting firms, and we believe that book can double. The growth won't come from renewals that run themselves. It will come from moving customers onto our AI and Agents platform, defending against cheaper point solutions and free AI tools, and handling firms that keep acquiring each other.

As Senior Manager, Account Management – EMEA, you'll lead a team of 5 Account Managers, report to our EMEA Sales leader, and own retention, expansion and forecast accuracy for the region. This is a player-coach role in spirit. You'll be in the deals and in front of senior partners and executives, not managing from a dashboard.

Why DataSnipper

The best commercial opportunities don't come around every day. Selling technology that's transforming an entire industry is one of them.

We believe trust is essential to how society works. Every day, we rely on information that's been independently verified, from financial statements to the products we buy, to the sustainability claims companies make. Behind that trust are audit and finance professionals who examine evidence, verify information and hold organizations accountable.

At DataSnipper, we build AI solutions that empower those professionals to make those judgements. With Alwin by DataSnipper, our new agentic platform, AI agents now take on end-to-end audit and finance procedures, while every conclusion stays traceable to its source. That frees professionals to focus on the judgment and expertise that make their work so important.

We're trusted by Fortune 500 companies, government agencies and all Big Four audit firms. Today, more than 600,000 professionals across 3,000+ organizations in 175 countries rely on our platform, and in 2025 alone DataSnipper delivered more than $1.4 billion in productivity savings to its customers.

Backed by a $100 million Series B led by Index Ventures, at a $1 billion valuation, we've built a strong foundation for what's next. And as proud members of 1% for the Planet, we care about how we grow, not just how fast.

For our commercial teams, this is where things get exciting.

Alwin has just launched, demand is growing, and we're expanding into new markets and segments. With a product customers already rely on, there's a huge opportunity to make your mark.

If you're commercially driven, ambitious, and excited to build something bigger, this is you chance to help shape the future of audit and finance and accelerate your own career along the way.

What You Will Do

Lead and Build the Team

  • Lead, coach and develop a team of 5 AMs, with hands-on deal coaching on renewal strategy, negotiation and executive engagement

  • Raise the talent bar: make the calls on the existing team and hire native speakers for under-covered markets (Dutch, German, French, Spanish)

  • Rebalance books as account loads move from 200 per rep toward 110, so every AM has room to go deep

Own the Number

  • Bring a strategic lens to renewals: move customers up-market on packaging and from legacy products onto our AI platform

  • Lead high-stakes negotiations with senior partners and executives at Europe's leading accounting firms, including network and multi-entity agreements, price increases, multi-year commitments and competitive displacement threats

  • Build and present business cases that tie DataSnipper to the outcomes partners care about: audit quality, capacity, margin and talent retention. Business conversations, not feature walkthroughs

Build Forecast Discipline

  • Build a renewal and expansion forecasting method that sees at least a full quarter out (today we see 2 months), ideally run in Gong

  • Run the operating cadence with your team and the CS leaders: renewal reviews, deal rooms and pipeline inspection

Be the Voice of the EMEA Customer

  • Partner with Customer Success on adoption and risk, with Product on what customers need from Agents, and with Marketing on firm-level programs

  • Bring sharp, data-backed insight on churn risk, competitor activity and pricing pressure to senior leadership

What You Bring

  • 7+ years in B2B SaaS sales, with at least 2–3 years leading an Account Management or renewals/expansion team (team leads ready to step up are welcome)

  • A track record of renewing and expanding a product that didn't sell itself. We want commercial operators, not relationship managers

  • Strong negotiation skills: you trade concessions for commitments, you don't give too much too early, and you've negotiated directly with economic buyers

  • Credibility with senior executives: you've had business value conversations with partners, CFOs or managing directors and built business cases with real numbers that won their approval

  • Deep discovery skills: you ask the 2nd, 3rd and 4th question until you reach the real business problem

  • A forecasting method you've actually run, and the discipline to inspect it weekly

  • Urgency and a competitive streak. You'd rather get on a plane to see the customer than send another email

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer - Alwin
jobs.description:
We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer in our Amsterdam office to build Alwin, our Agentic Automation Platform for audit and finance, and the systems around it. Alwin agents run multi-step audit procedures over client evidence and return finished workpapers with every number traced back to source. Humans plan, review and sign off.

This is a hands-on role: most of your time will be spent writing code, building the hardest parts of the runtime, prototyping new capabilities and getting them into production. You lead by example: engineers follow your direction because they see it work in your code. Your impact will also come through the engineers and teams you work with.

Your mission is to build the best agentic runtime for audit: one that completes audit tasks faster, more accurately, more reliably and at lower cost, while scaling to meet the needs of our largest customers.

You will identify the problems that most constrain that mission, align teams around a technical direction and drive solutions through to measurable results, while building the foundations other engineers use and raising the quality of Alwin’s agents in production.

Why DataSnipper?

The hardest AI problems aren't about getting an answer fast. They're about getting one people can trust.

We believe trust is essential to how society works. Every day, we rely on information that's been independently verified, from financial statements to the products we buy, to the sustainability claims companies make. Behind that trust are audit and finance professionals who examine evidence, verify information and hold organizations accountable.

At DataSnipper, we build AI solutions that empower those professionals. By making evidence easier to trace and verify, we help them focus on the judgment and expertise that make their work so important.

For our product and engineering team, this is where things get exciting. In audit, a plausible answer isn't good enough. Every output has to be explainable and traceable back to its source. We've just launched a brand new agentic platform, Alwin by DataSnipper. AI agents running in the cloud across hundreds of documents at once, reasoning across PDF, Word and Excel, with a full audit trail behind every step. There are lots of greenfield problems ahead, and real room to shape what we build and how we build it.

And we build at scale. More than 600,000 professionals across 3,000+ organizations in 175 countries rely on DataSnipper, including Fortune 500 companies, government agencies and all Big Four audit firms. In 2025 alone, the DataSnipper platform delivered more than $1.4 billion in productivity savings to is customers. Backed by a $100 million Series B led by Index Ventures, at a $1 billion valuation, and as proud members of 1% for the Planet, we care about how we grow, not just how fast.

If you want to build AI that professionals trust with work that really matters, this is your chance to help shape the future of audit and finance and do the best work of your career along the way.

What You Will Do:

Results You Will Drive

  • Better audit outcomes: improve how accurately and reliably agents complete real audit tasks, with traceable results and human oversight.

  • A faster, more efficient runtime: reduce execution time and cost while scaling to more complex workloads and larger customers.

  • More capable teams: build foundations and feedback loops that multiple teams use to ship and improve agents faster.

Build & Ship

  • Build proofs of concept for new agent capabilities, and take the ones that work all the way to production

  • Champion experimentation and R&D: try emerging models and techniques, solve hard problems creatively, and turn promising ideas into reliable features

  • Build shared capabilities that multiple teams adopt, and remain accountable for whether they make those teams faster and their products more reliable

  • Contribute directly to the agent harness at the core of Alwin: the orchestration, tools, context and evaluation loops every agent runs on

  • Anticipate where the platform needs to be in 12 to 18 months, and make design decisions now that minimize the cost of future change

Agents in Production

  • Build agents that are reliable in a regulated domain: grounding, evaluation before release, human-in-the-loop, traceability of every action

  • Improve how teams build Alwin by establishing tooling and feedback loops that help them detect agent failures, prioritize improvements, prevent regressions and ship production-ready agents faster

  • Jump into the hardest incidents across teams, resolve immediate problems and turn what you learn into lasting, systemic fixes

jobs.title: Bookkeeper (Boekhouder)
jobs.description:
Monumental is automating on-site construction with robotics and software. Our mission is to make construction software-defined and autonomous - a future where beautiful, bespoke buildings go up in a single day, with minimal labour.

We're a growing team of engineers, operators and technicians from diverse backgrounds, including consumer tech, finance and media, and companies like Dyson, Shopify, Meta and Tesla. It's still the early days of building the company, and this is a chance to make an outsized impact on a problem that matters. From day one, you'll be working with an experienced founding team, backed by a $32M Series B led by Khosla Ventures and Plural, alongside other renowned investors.

Monumental is based in the city centre of Amsterdam, in a beautiful facility with a fully equipped workshop and robot testing floor. We build the whole stack in-house, hardware and software. Our work involves building robots in our workshop and houses on real construction sites, so we're onsite five days a week.

Read more on why we believe you should spend your time working on construction, and learn about our vision and company. You might enjoy our YouTube Channel, Based in Europe’s film on how we’re fixing Europe’s housing shortage, or this video by Andreas Klinger of what our office looks like.

About the role

We're looking for a Bookkeeper to bring our day-to-day bookkeeping and month-end close in-house. You'll be our first dedicated bookkeeper, taking over from our external accounting firm and running the books for our growing group: five Dutch BVs today, plus our entities abroad.

Our transaction volume has roughly doubled this year, and 2027 is the first financial year our accounts will be audited. You'll own the reconciliations, records and close process that make our numbers reliable, working closely with our finance lead, purchasing team and external accountants. The external accountants will continue to handle annual accounts and corporate tax, with local advisors handling tax filings abroad.

This is a hands-on bookkeeping role for someone with at least three years of experience running the full cycle through month-end. Our data and processes need cleaning up. If you enjoy turning a messy administration into a tidy one, this is that job. As you settle in, there is room to take on VAT filing and monthly payroll processing.

The role is based at our Amsterdam HQ, on-site five days a week. Salary is up to €50,000 gross a year, including the 8% holiday allowance.

What you'll do

  • Own daily bookkeeping. Code supplier invoices and card spend in Spendesk with the right GL account, VAT code and cost centre, and post them to the general ledger without re-keying. Keep supplier records clean and prepare payment runs. Supplier bank-detail changes are independently verified and approved; payment approval and release sit with the finance lead.

  • Keep accounts reconciled. Reconcile bank accounts, keep payables and receivables current, and investigate outstanding items so every balance is supported or explained.

  • Run the month-end close. Close all entities to a fixed timetable, initially by working day eight and moving towards working day five. Own accruals, prepayments and balance-sheet reconciliations, collect or prepare foreign entities' figures, agree intercompany balances and reconcile group reporting to the ledgers.

  • Maintain fixed assets and inventory records. Keep the fixed-asset register up to date, including capitalisation and depreciation of our robot fleet under agreed accounting policies, and reconcile inventory accounts to month-end stock values.

  • Prepare Dutch VAT returns. Prepare quarterly btw returns with our external accountants reviewing, and take over filing them over time.

  • Keep the books audit-ready. Maintain supporting schedules and an audit file throughout the year. Be a day-to-day contact for our external accountants and support the audit of our 2027 accounts.

  • Improve how we work. Document the close, fix recurring errors and use spreadsheets, software and AI tools to reduce manual work while checking the results carefully. Depending on your experience, take on payroll processing in Loket over time, with payroll tax filings remaining with our external accountants.

What we're looking for

  • Full-cycle bookkeeping experience. You have at least three years of experience running the books through month-end, at an accounting firm (accountantskantoor) or in-house.

  • Hands-on Dutch VAT experience. You've prepared Dutch btw returns and can work through the supporting records.

  • Strong reconciliation skills. You've handled balance-sheet reconciliations, accruals and prepayments, beyond processing invoices. You investigate differences and follow them through to a resolution.

  • Accuracy and ownership. You keep records organised, meet close deadlines and raise missing information or accounting questions early. You'd rather find the €12 difference than book it to suspense.

  • Fluent English and professional working Dutch. English is our working language, and your manager doesn't speak Dutch. You can independently read and process Dutch invoices, tax correspondence and payroll documents.

  • Comfort with systems and confidential information. You work confidently with spreadsheets, learn new accounting tools and handle financial and employee information carefully.

  • Nice to have: Twinfield, Basecone or Spendesk (Exact, Odoo or similar also counts); multi-entity or multi-country bookkeeping, intercompany and consolidation; fixed-asset or inventory accounting in hardware or manufacturing; statutory audit support; Dutch payroll experience, ideally in Loket; an accounting qualification such as MBO-4/HBO, SPD or Praktijkdiploma Boekhouden; experience automating repetitive work.

Why Monumental?

Joining Monumental means being at the forefront of a movement aimed at making significant strides in the construction industry. Here, your work has the potential to impact not just the company but the future of how we build. If you're driven by innovation, eager to tackle complex challenges, and ready to make a tangible difference, we want to hear from you.

For open applications (where you don't see an exact role match), please reach out to us at:

Unfortunately we do not currently support internships.

If you don't meet all the qualifications here but are excited about Monumental and feel you'd still be able to help us tackle complex challenges, do get in touch. We welcome generalists who focus on outcomes and are eager to learn on the job.

About myTomorrows 

myTomorrows is a global health tech company dedicated to breaking down barriers for patients seeking treatment options.   

We strive to enable earlier and better treatment access by bridging the gap between those searching for possible options, and the companies who develop them. We work closely with patients, healthcare professionals, trial sites, patient advocacy groups, and BioPharma – connecting key stakeholders in the drug development ecosystem.   

We’ve developed a cutting-edge AI-powered technology platform that simplifies and streamlines access to drugs in development. To support our users and clients, we have a range of industry-expert specialized teams ready to help. Our services include clinical trial patient recruitment, Expanded Access Program management and Real-World Data collection.   

With a global footprint spanning 134 countries, to date we’ve supported over 17,000 patients, 3,000 physicians and 350 sites, earning the trust of 60+ BioPharma companies. In October 2025, we closed a €25M investment with Avego Healthcare Capital to fuel our global ambitions and scale the business.  

Join us in shaping the future of treatment access - making tomorrow’s therapies accessible for people who need them today.

jobs.title: System Architect
jobs.description:
Hyperscale Power is building the power backbone for the AI data center era: a complete power conversion chain from 13.8kV–35kV medium-voltage AC down to 800V DC, combining ultra-compact SiC-based power blocks. Our Solid-State Transformers (SSTs) are the core of this revolution, providing unprecedented control, efficiency, and compactness.

As a System Architect, you will be responsible for our solid-state transformer as a complete system. You will connect the work of our power electronics, magnetics, and mechanical and thermal engineering teams into one coherent system, and ensure it meets the requirements of hyperscale data center customers.

Instead of specializing in a single subsystem, your mission is to keep the whole system in view: balancing efficiency, size, cost, reliability and manufacturability, guiding the key technical trade-offs, and taking our SST from prototype to a product ready for certification and series production.

This role is for you if…
you’ve owned a complex high-power system rather than one part of it. You enjoy keeping the whole picture in view, making the call on trade-offs between expert teams, and bringing just enough structure to a fast-moving team without slowing it down.

This role isn’t for you if…
you’ve spent your career going deep on a single component or subsystem, or you manage projects without making the technical decisions yourself. It’s also not a fit if you need a fixed specification and established processes before you can start.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the system architecture of the SST and its key performance metrics, including efficiency, power density, cost, thermal performance, reliability, manufacturability and control performance.

  • Coordinate the subsystems of the SST (AC/DC, DC/DC, magnetics, mechanical and thermal) and their interfaces, ensuring the work of each team is compatible and consistent with the system design.

  • Lead system-level trade-off decisions and set technical priorities across teams.

  • Define and maintain system requirements, interface specifications and change management, ensuring design changes are assessed for their impact across the system.

  • Translate the requirements of data center operators and hyperscalers into system specifications, and track how they evolve.

  • Explore and compare different system architectures and their integration in the datacenter power supply chain

  • Drive standardization and design for manufacturing across subsystems in preparation for series production.

  • Work with the compliance and certification team to define a feasible certification path for the system.

  • Identify technical risks at system level early and propose mitigations.

Qualifications

  • MSc or a higher degree in Electrical Engineering or a related discipline.

  • 8+ years of industry experience in developing complex power electronic systems.

  • Proven responsibility at system or platform level, e.g. as system engineer, system architect, technical lead or team lead.

  • Track record of taking power electronic systems from development to series product.

  • Experience with high-power systems such as EV charging, electric drivetrains, rail traction, industrial drives, renewable energy converters or robotics.

  • Broad understanding of the electrical, magnetic, thermal, mechanical and control aspects of power electronic systems, and how they interact.

  • Working knowledge of cooling concepts and the mechanical integration of high-power electronics.

  • Experience with standards, norms and certification processes for power electronic products.

  • Strong communication and decision-making skills; able to align experts across disciplines and drive decisions.

  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced startup environment with evolving requirements.

The job will be located at our HQ in Egg b. Zürich, Switzerland.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with medium-voltage converter systems or solid-state transformers.

  • Knowledge of data center power architectures.

  • Experience in design for manufacturing and cost engineering.

  • Experience establishing systems engineering processes in a growing organization.

Benefits

We’re a diverse team, and we want everyone to feel comfortable being themselves at work. If you want to grow fast, learn constantly and help shape where we go next, we’d love to hear from you.

About the role

Every enterprise wants to be AI-ready, and most are held back by legacy data estates built over decades. As Enterprise Migrations Practice Area Lead, you’ll own how Infinite Lambda solves that problem: moving the world’s largest organisations off Informatica, Talend, SSIS/SQL Server, DataStage, stored procedures and, increasingly, SAS and Alteryx, onto modern platforms ready for AI.

Enterprise migrations are a core pillar of our growth strategy, and this role sets the standard for how we deliver them globally. The practice spans the full migration lifecycle:

  • Assess: Estate discovery, feasibility analysis and migration strategy, ending in a fixed-cost, fixed-timeline proposal that gives clients certainty from day one.

  • Convert: Automated code conversion with Flowline, our proprietary product, which combines deterministic and LLM-assisted methods. This stage also covers refactoring, optimisation and a first-pass ontology that lays the foundation for AI use cases.

  • Validate: Reconciliation architecture and row-level sign-off, so every migration is provably correct.

The first part is delivery excellence that compounds. You’ll make sure every migration we deliver is better than the last. That means defining the standards, building the playbooks and reusable assets, and turning the lessons from each strategic engagement into capability across the practice. You’ll also develop the engineers and leads who carry that standard across AMER, EMEA and APAC.

The second part is commercial impact. You’ll turn delivery quality into a competitive edge: faster delivery, sharper scoping and pricing, and healthy margins you can measure and report on. Working closely with Sales and Solution Engineering, you’ll shape the offer that makes Infinite Lambda the obvious choice for enterprise migration, anywhere in the world.

1. Practice and standards

  • Be the person engineers, sales and clients ask when a migration question is hard: what to migrate first, what to refactor and what to move as is, and how to resolve conflicting logic.

  • Own the migration standard for Assess, Convert and Validate. This covers reference architectures, sequencing, reconciliation and stage-gate checklists, and what we won’t do.

  • Make sure Fast and Deep Discovery produce a defensible estimate, a dependency map and early red flags before we commit to a fixed price.

  • Hold the same quality bar in every region: conversion quality, reconciliation sign-off and post-go-live incidents.

  • Keep the practice up to date as Flowline, the source parsers and the target platforms change (Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Iceberg).

2. Knowledge, IP and the asset catalogue

  • Join engagements at scoping and agree what each strategic migration should leave behind (patterns, decisions, failure modes, measurements) and who will capture it.

  • Capture lessons at wave checkpoints, and close each engagement with a review of what worked, what didn’t, and what should change in the standard.

  • Decide which lessons become reusable assets and which stay one-offs.

  • Bring field requirements and recurring challanges to the Flowline product team, and move proven assets into Product & Services.

3. People and enablement

  • Build a global bench of migration specialists. Develop engineers across AMER, EMEA and APAC into a team that can deliver migration waves to our standard, independently and at scale.

  • Own the path from practitioner to leader. Design and run the progression that takes engineers from dbt and Snowflake foundations, through Flowline accreditation and deep expertise in a legacy source system, to owning delivery waves and ultimately leading client assessments.

  • Turn what we know into how we work. Make our accelerators and existing assets visible and reusable across every team, so each engagement starts from our best work rather than a blank page.

4. Commercial

  • Make sure live engagements actually use the practice’s accelerators.

  • Help Sales and Sales Engineers scope, estimate and price from measured delivery speed, so the client pays for the acceleration instead of getting it for free.

  • Make the commercial case for the practice in proposals, extensions and new scope. This includes turning Discovery engagements into migrations and expanding into BI and semantic-layer work.

  • Act as the technical lead in joint pursuits with Snowflake, Databricks, dbt and Fivetran, and feed what we learn in delivery into joint go-to-market, certifications and co-marketing.

  • Write interview material and run technical interviews for migration roles.

  • Present the practice’s work inside the company and, where it makes sense, at external events and in case studies.

  • Ownership at a strategic level. You take full accountability for outcomes, not just tasks. You’ve owned a practice, a service line or a major programme end to end (its direction, quality, people and commercial results), and you’re comfortable making the calls that shape how a business delivers.

  • Enterprise migration experience at scale. You have a track record of leading large, complex migrations off legacy platforms such as Informatica, Talend, Oracle, SSIS or DataStage, and you know where these programmes tend to go wrong.

  • Depth across both ends of the migration. You have hands-on knowledge of legacy source systems and modern platforms (Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Iceberg, dbt, Fivetran), plus a structured approach to assessment, conversion and validation.

  • A builder of repeatable delivery. You’ve defined reference architectures, sequencing frameworks and quality gates, and built libraries of reusable assets and accelerators that teams actually use.

  • Credibility with clients and partners. You can lead discovery sessions with senior client stakeholders, act as the technical lead in joint pursuits with partners such as Snowflake and Databricks, and assess engineering talent in interviews.

  • Commercial awareness. You understand how delivery choices affect scoping, pricing and margin, and you enjoy working with Sales to win the right work.

Your line manager is the Chief Customer Success Officer, who is accountable for your direction, the practice charter and the review of your objectives. Strategic direction will be consulted with CTO and Head of Engineering.

Why join Infinite Lambda

Creative Director

Build with us

Businesses deserve better from finance. Less friction, more freedom. Since 2004, Mollie has been on a mission to make payments and money management effortless for every business in Europe.

Today, more than 250,000 companies trust our all-in-one platform to get paid, manage money and grow on their terms. Simple, scalable and built with real businesses in mind.

If you’re ready to grow, shape the future of fintech and join an ambitious, high-performing team, this is the place for you.

The job is to balance craft excellence with speed and scale.

Brand Design is a core enabler of our GTM and growth. You'll build a consistent, world-class brand experience across our platforms and markets, so the businesses we serve understand and choose Mollie. You'll own the evolution of our visual identity, design systems and creative principles, and act as the quality bar for all brand output, with executive backing to shape how Mollie shows up everywhere, including as we expand.

You'll work with Marketing Operations on workflows and tooling, and bring in AI tools to speed up ideation, production and iteration without lowering the bar. You'll also collaborate with teams like Employee Experience and Internal Events, and manage external agencies, freelancers and production partners when needed.

What you'll ship

  • A clear, evolved brand design vision, plus a refreshed visual identity and design system that markets adopt consistently.

  • A high-performing, well-structured in-house studio, with the workflows, tooling and modular systems to deliver high-quality output at scale.

  • Impactful end to end creative for flagship campaigns, product launches and brand moments that is on-brand, insight-driven and effective.

  • AI-enabled creative workflows that measurably increase speed and output while holding the quality bar.

  • Strong creative partnership with Marketing, Product, Growth and leadership, including a meaningful uplift to performance marketing creative.

  • In your first 90 days: an assessment of the team, output and brand system, a defined vision and quick wins delivered.

  • Within 6 to 12 months: a scaled studio operating model, the evolved identity live in market and AI workflows embedded.

What you'll bring

  • Proven experience leading and scaling in-house design teams or creative studios, including people leadership of a multidisciplinary team. You inspire, challenge and develop designers at all levels.

  • A strong portfolio that shows high-quality brand, campaign and digital work, backed by proven brand craft.

  • Exceptional creative judgement and taste, and a clear point of view on what "great" looks like.

  • Experience building and maintaining design systems and brand frameworks that scale for consistency and self-serve.

  • Operational strength in planning, prioritization, resourcing and workflow design, so quality holds at scale.

  • Hands-on experience applying AI in creative workflows, including concepting, production and scaling assets.

  • Strong communication and storytelling, with the ability to explain creative decisions to senior stakeholders, and fluent English.

Grow your way

At Mollie, growth is personal. We believe everyone should have the chance to develop their skills, explore new challenges and shape their career on their own terms.

In this role, you’ll have the unique opportunity to build a meaningful distribution channel from the ground up. As we expand across Europe, you will grow alongside the product area you own. You’ll get regular feedback and performance reviews to support your development, with fair and transparent salary reviews along the way.

Unlock your full potential and join us to eliminate financial bureaucracy

jobs.title: IT & Cloud Manager (m/w/d)
jobs.description:
IT & Cloud Manager (m/w/d)

Krumbach-Niederraunau, Bayern · Hybrid · Vollzeit, unbefristet

Über Everfield

Everfield übernimmt, entwickelt und skaliert europäische Softwareunternehmen aus vertikalen Märkten und Spezialnischen und gibt ihnen die Werkzeuge an die Hand, um den nächsten Schritt zu gehen. Unsere Mission: Ambitionen fördern, Wachstum vorantreiben und Chancen für Europas Software-Ökosystem eröffnen.

Die Unternehmen im Everfield-Ökosystem arbeiten dezentral: Sie behalten ihre Teams, Marken und Standorte und konzentrieren sich auf das, was sie am besten können – Produkte entwickeln und Kunden betreuen. Everfield unterstützt mit Talent Acquisition, HR und einem Expertenteam, das zu Finanz- und Operations-Themen berät. Seit der Gründung 2022 ist Everfield in neun Ländern vertreten, Tendenz steigend.

Über SoCom

Die SoCom Informationssysteme GmbH entwickelt mit rund 45 Mitarbeitenden TIKOS, die führende ERP-Lösung für gewerbliche Wäschereien und Textildienstleister. Mit rund 40 % Marktanteil in der DACH-Region und über 30 Jahren Erfahrung steuern Kunden mit TIKOS ihre gesamte Prozesskette, von der Wäscheannahme über RFID-Tracking bis zur Auslieferung. Seit Oktober 2026 gehört auch die Düchting Software & Consulting GmbH zur SoCom-Familie. SoCom ist Teil des Everfield-Ökosystems.

Über die Rolle

Du übernimmst die Verantwortung für unsere gesamte IT: die interne Infrastruktur, die Informationssicherheit und die SoCom Cloud, in der wir TIKOS für unsere Kunden betreiben. Viele dieser Leistungen haben wir bisher extern eingekauft. Jetzt holen wir das Know-how ins Haus – und du stellst die IT so auf, dass sie mit unserem Wachstum, der Integration neuer Unternehmensteile und steigenden regulatorischen Anforderungen Schritt hält.

Du bist Gestalter:in und Macher:in zugleich: Du entwickelst die IT-Strategie gemeinsam mit der Geschäftsführung und packst im Tagesgeschäft selbst mit an.

Deine Aufgaben

• IT-Verantwortung und Strategie: Du verantwortest die IT von SoCom ganzheitlich, entwickelst gemeinsam mit der Geschäftsführung eine IT-Roadmap und steuerst das IT-Budget für Hardware, Lizenzen, Cloud und Dienstleister.

• Insourcing und Dienstleistersteuerung: Du überführst bisher extern erbrachte Leistungen – Netzwerk, Firewall, Server, Backup und E-Mail-Security – schrittweise in die eigene Verantwortung. Verbleibende Dienstleister und Verträge steuerst du über klare SLAs.

• Cloud und Hosting: Du betreibst die SoCom Cloud, in der wir TIKOS für Kunden hosten, und entwickelst sie weiter. Gemeinsam mit Vertrieb und Support kalkulierst du Hosting-Angebote, verantwortest Verfügbarkeit, Kapazität und Kosten und treibst eine zukunftsfähige Hosting-Architektur voran.

• Infrastruktur und Betrieb: Du verantwortest Server, Netzwerk, Firewall, Backup und Disaster Recovery – am Standort und in der Cloud – sowie Microsoft 365, Endgeräte, Telefonie und Mobilfunk. Monitoring und Patch-Management steuerst du über ein RMM-Tool.

• Informationssicherheit und Compliance: Als interne:r Owner für IT-Security koordinierst du das Schwachstellen- und Incident-Management, arbeitest eng mit dem CISO-Netzwerk von Everfield zusammen und setzt die Anforderungen aus NIS-2, Cyber Resilience Act und DSGVO in der Infrastruktur um.

• Integration Düchting: Du bringst die IT der Düchting Software & Consulting GmbH bis 2027 auf SoCom-Standard und konsolidierst Systeme, Lizenzen und Prozesse.

• Dokumentation und Wissenssicherung: Du baust eine belastbare IT-Dokumentation auf – Systeme, Zugänge, Kosten und Notfallpläne –, damit Wissen im Team geteilt und jederzeit verfügbar ist.

• Führung und Zusammenarbeit: Du arbeitest eng mit unserer IT-Administration zusammen und bildest mit ihr ein Team mit gegenseitiger Vertretung. Für Support, R&D, DevOps und Vertrieb bist du die zentrale Ansprechperson für alle IT-Themen.

• KI und Digitalisierung: Du begleitest den sicheren Einsatz von KI-Tools im Unternehmen gemäß der KI-Richtlinie von Everfield und automatisierst interne IT-Prozesse.

Was du mitbringst

Muss

• Abgeschlossenes Studium (Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik o. Ä.) oder Ausbildung zur/zum Fachinformatiker:in mit entsprechender Berufserfahrung

• Mindestens 5 Jahre Erfahrung in der IT-Administration oder im IT-Management, davon mindestens 2 Jahre in verantwortlicher Rolle in einem mittelständischen Unternehmen (ca. 30–250 Mitarbeitende)

• Fundierte Praxis mit Windows Server, Active Directory/Entra ID, Microsoft 365, Netzwerken (VLAN, VPN) und Firewalls (z. B. Sophos, Fortinet)

• Erfahrung im Betrieb von Cloud- oder Hosting-Infrastruktur (IaaS, z. B. IONOS, Azure, AWS) inklusive Virtualisierung, Backup und Disaster Recovery

• Ausgeprägtes Sicherheitsbewusstsein und praktische Erfahrung im Schwachstellen- und Incident-Management

• Erfahrung in der Steuerung externer IT-Dienstleister sowie im Budget- und Lizenzmanagement

• Hands-on-Mentalität: Du übernimmst Verantwortung und löst Probleme selbst

• Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau und gute Englischkenntnisse für die Abstimmung im internationalen Everfield-Netzwerk

Kann

• Erfahrung im Hosting von Business-Software für externe Kunden (SLAs, Mandantentrennung)

• Kenntnisse in NIS-2, ISO 27001/BSI IT-Grundschutz oder dem Cyber Resilience Act

• Erfahrung mit SQL-Server-Datenbanken und Linux-Systemen

• Erfahrung mit RMM-Tools (z. B. NinjaOne, Datto RMM) und Automatisierung mit PowerShell

• Erfahrung mit IT-Integrationen nach Unternehmenszukäufen

• Kenntnisse im sicheren Einsatz von KI-Tools

Nicht jede:r erfüllt jeden Punkt. Wenn du die Muss-Kriterien weitgehend mitbringst und Lust auf die Aufgabe hast, bewirb dich – wir freuen uns, dich kennenzulernen.

Bewerbungsprozess

• Erstgespräch (30 Min.) mit Karolina, Talent Acquisition Partner bei Everfield

• Fachinterview (60 Min.) mit Stefan Hoffmann, Geschäftsführer SoCom, und Everfield AI Lead

• Finales Gespräch vor Ort in Krumbach (90 Min.) mit Fallstudie (z. B. ein Insourcing-Plan für einen externen IT-Dienstleister) und Kennenlernen des Teams

Die Position ist hybrid mit regelmäßiger Präsenz an unserem Standort in Krumbach-Niederraunau

Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung!

jobs.title: Senior AI R&D Engineer – Model Training  (f/m/d)
jobs.description:
Our Mission

Aleph Alpha is one of the few companies in Europe doing serious foundation model pre-training like our recently released Kolibri-1 model. Our customers - in finance, manufacturing, public administration - need models that understand German, meet European regulatory requirements, and work reliably in high-stakes settings. We're building that in Heidelberg.

Team Culture

At Aleph Alpha, we foster a culture built on ownership, autonomy, and empowerment. Teams and individual contributors are trusted to take responsibility for their work and drive meaningful impact. We maintain a flat organizational structure with efficient, supportive management that enables quick decision-making, open communication, and a strong sense of shared purpose.

We believe a strong engineering culture is the key to model training success. We like Extreme Programming and favor trunk-based development. We often mob-program, which keeps us aligned and means we always learn from each other.

About the Role

As a Senior AI R&D Engineer in Model Training (f/m/d), you will join our model training team in Heidelberg or Berlin. Most of the team is based in Heidelberg. The model training team is building and improving our model training pipeline, which has been used to train Kolibri.

  • You will work across our full stack. Some weeks you might be optimizing how training loads are scheduled on our cluster and making the pipeline more robust and performant so we can iterate faster. Other weeks, you will be enabling large-scale code execution for reinforcement learning. And at other times, you might dig deep into our evaluation codebase to lift inference throughput on evals.

  • No two days are the same. Things move fast, and your ability to focus and prioritize is what lets you unblock the team day-to-day while designing the high-quality tooling and infrastructure that speeds us up long-term.

  • We're still building out our training pipeline and infrastructure. Some pieces exist, some do not, and you will have real influence on what gets built and how. Your work directly shapes how quickly we can experiment and improve our models.

  • Identifying issues and taking initiative is what drives our day-to-day work.

  • Working mode, design decisions, priorities are all done in your team together with your team mates.
    The strongest teams often use highly collaborative techniques, like mob or pair programming.

  • Due to the highly collaborative nature of our work you are expected to be on-site at least two days a week. If you are in Berlin, you should expect to travel around every second month for a few days to Heidelberg.

  • We are specifically looking to strengthen the Software Engineering in the teams which are research heavy. Major points include improving the maintainability of our code through tests and design & architecture changes.

Requirements

  • At its core, you need to be able to dive into a codebase, change the behavior as necessary, and after the change the code should be better tested and easier to understand than before.

  • As such we look for candidates for an understanding of how to design for low coupling and high cohesion paired with the ability to incrementally refactor.

  • Experience with the following technologies is likely to be helpful:

    • Test Driven Development (TDD)

    • Trunk based development

    • Continuous integration

    • Domain Driven Design

Nice-to-haves

  • Most of our code is in Python, there is also the occasional Rust codebase.

  • Large parts of our training pipeline are built on top of Kubernetes.

  • We do not hire for skills in a particular technology or language, but rather ability to learn and mindset, yet experience with these technologies is a plus.

What we offer

  • Become part of an AI revolution!

  • 30 days of paid vacation

  • Access to a variety of fitness & wellness offerings via Wellhub

  • Mental health support through nilo.health

  • Substantially subsidized company pension plan for your future security

  • Subsidized Germany-wide transportation ticket

  • Budget for additional technical equipment

  • Flexible working hours for better work-life balance and hybrid working model

  • JobRad® Bike Lease
